transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I keep eating in the evenings until I'm so full it's uncomfortable, even when I don't really want more. Some folks in my church small group encouraged me to come speak to someone about it. It's just gotten to a point where I'm pretty embarrassed by how I'm acting around food lately.
Do you usually feel a sense of guilt or self-criticism after these episodes of eating until you're uncomfortably full?

Yes, I do. I sit there in the quiet house looking at the empty containers and dirty dishes, feeling completely gross and ashamed. I end up beating myself up that a grown man who used to run tight truck routes on a strict schedule can't even control what he puts in his own mouth.
During these episodes of eating, do you feel like you're unable to stop once you've started, or is it more that you're intentionally trying to comfort yourself or fill a void?

It probably started as a way to fill the quiet of the empty house after my divorce, but once I actually start eating, it feels completely out of my control. It’s like I’m watching myself grab one thing after another, telling myself, "Magin, stop, you don’t need this," but I just can’t stop until it’s all gone or I’m hurting.
How often do these episodes of uncontrollable eating occur, and have they been happening regularly over time or are they more sporadic?

They've been happening pretty much every night, at least several times a week without any real break. This has been going on consistently for about the last three months, starting right around when my divorce was finalized and I transitioned to my new office role.
Can you estimate how much of your daily caloric intake is consumed during these evening episodes, and has your overall weight changed significantly since they started?

I'm not really sure about the exact calorie count, though I know it's a massive amount of food to eat in one sitting. I also haven't stepped on a scale lately, so I'm not sure if my weight has changed much since this all started.
Have you experienced any episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period of time during the day, or are these episodes exclusively occurring in the evenings?

No, these episodes happen exclusively in the evenings. During the day, I'm kept pretty busy with my mentoring and office work, so I do just fine then. But once I get home to the quiet house and cook dinner, that's when the overeating starts.

Can you describe if there are any specific emotions or events that trigger these episodes of uncontrollable eating in the evenings, and do you experience a sense of loss of control during these episodes?

The big triggers are the quietness and loneliness of my empty house, which has been really hard since my divorce, my youngest moving out, and shifting away from the busy routine of long-haul driving. Once I start eating, I absolutely lose control—it feels like something else takes over and I just can't stop myself, even when I'm telling myself to stop.

Can you tell me more about how long these episodes of uncontrollable eating last, from the moment you start eating until you finally stop, and have you noticed any pattern or consistency in their duration?

To be honest, I'm not entirely sure of the exact timeframe since I haven't really timed them. I just know that I eat very quickly, almost shoveling the food down, until I'm painfully full and finally have to stop.

Have you been experiencing any other symptoms like persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, or changes in your sleep patterns or energy levels, alongside these episodes of uncontrollable eating?

I definitely feel down and really sluggish the morning after a bad night of overeating, but I'm not sure about overall depression. I still enjoy getting out to garden or fish when I can, and my sleep seems okay other than just feeling heavy and tired from all that food.

Can you clarify if the feeling of loss of control during these eating episodes is specifically related to the emotional distress you're experiencing, such as the loneliness and quietness of the house, or if it seems more like a physical or compulsive aspect of the eating itself?

It's really a combination of both. The eating initially starts as a way to cope with the quietness and loneliness of the empty house after my divorce and my youngest leaving. But once I actually start, it transitions into a compulsive state where it feels like something takes over and I'm just watching myself helplessly eat, unable to stop even when I tell myself to.

Do you think the emotional distress you're experiencing, such as loneliness and feelings of emptiness, would improve if you were able to control your eating, or do you feel like the eating is a symptom of a deeper emotional issue that would still be present even if the eating were under control?

I think the eating is definitely a symptom of a deeper issue, because the loneliness and emptiness really started with my divorce, my youngest moving away, and coming home to a quiet house after years on the road. While controlling the eating would stop the immediate shame and physical discomfort, that quietness and empty house would still be there. I'd still have to face that underlying emptiness.

Have you considered or tried any other coping mechanisms for dealing with the loneliness and emptiness, such as therapy, support groups, or hobbies, besides eating, and if so, how have they helped or not helped?

I still enjoy hobbies like fishing and gardening, but lately, even evenings that start with those activities and cooking just end up leading into my overeating. I do attend a church small group, and after I finally admitted my embarrassment to them, their encouragement is what prompted me to seek professional help today. I haven't tried any formal therapy or other support groups before this.

You mentioned you still enjoy activities like gardening or fishing, but have you noticed any decrease in the pleasure you derive from these activities since your divorce and the onset of your eating issues?

I haven't really thought about it, but I don't think I've noticed a decrease in the pleasure I get from fishing or gardening themselves. I still enjoy doing them when I can, but the real trouble always starts afterward once I'm back home in the evenings.

Can you clarify if you've experienced a significant decrease in interest or pleasure from activities other than gardening and fishing since your divorce, or if it's primarily the evening periods that are problematic for you?

It is primarily the evenings that are the problem for me. I still enjoy my hobbies, but I've started turning down invites to grab dinner or watch the game with my buddies because I'm too embarrassed about my eating habits and feel so sluggish the next morning. It's not that I've lost interest in hanging out with them, I'm just hiding how bad things have gotten.

Do you think that if you were able to find alternative ways to cope with the loneliness and emptiness, such as through therapy or support groups, you would be able to reduce the frequency or intensity of these episodes of uncontrollable eating?

That really hits close to home, as I've just been using food to fill the quiet and loneliness of my empty house since my divorce and my youngest kid moving out. Talking to my church small group is what got me to seek help in the first place, so I am definitely open to therapy or support. I really want to find better ways to cope with these empty evenings.

You've mentioned still enjoying activities like gardening and fishing, but have you noticed any decrease in interest or pleasure in social activities or other hobbies outside of these since your divorce and the onset of eating issues?

Yes, I've definitely been pulling away from social things, like turning down invites to grab dinner or watch the game with my buddies from the yard. I'm just so embarrassed by my eating habits, and I feel too sluggish and worn out the next morning after stuffing myself to face anyone. It's really keeping me isolated because I'm just hiding how bad things have gotten.

Do you think your uncontrollable eating episodes would significantly decrease if your underlying emotional issues, such as loneliness and emptiness, were addressed and improved, or do you believe the eating behavior has become a separate, more compulsive issue that would persist regardless of emotional improvement?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest, because I haven't really thought about it in that way yet. While the quiet and loneliness of the house definitely trigger the eating, it currently feels like a powerful habit that just takes over once I start. I'm not sure if fixing the emotional side would completely stop that urge on its own.

Do you think that if you were able to effectively manage your feelings of loneliness and emptiness through other means, such as therapy or support, you would still experience the urge to engage in these episodes of uncontrollable eating?

That makes a lot of sense, as I definitely started eating to fill the quiet and loneliness of the house after my divorce and my youngest child moved out. While managing those feelings would probably help, right now the urge feels so powerful and automatic—like something just takes over—that it's hard to imagine how to stop it once it starts.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, outside of gardening and fishing, since your divorce and the onset of eating issues?

I still enjoy gardening and fishing when I can, but I've definitely stopped doing other social activities I used to love, like grabbing dinner or watching the game with my buddies from the yard. It's not because I've lost interest in those things, but rather because I feel too embarrassed about my eating habits and too sluggish the next morning after a night of overeating.

Can you clarify if the loss of interest in social activities, such as spending time with friends, is due to the embarrassment and guilt from overeating or if you've genuinely lost pleasure in these activities themselves?

It's definitely because of the embarrassment and how sluggish I feel, not because I've lost interest in the activities themselves. I would still love to hang out and watch the game with my buddies from the yard, but the shame of my evening eating and how worn out I am the next morning just keeps me from going.

Do you think the loss of control during these eating episodes is more closely related to the emotional distress you're experiencing, such as loneliness and feelings of emptiness, or is it more about a lack of control over your eating behavior itself?

It really feels like a combination of both. The urge to start eating usually comes from the loneliness and the quietness of the empty house after my divorce and my kid moving out. However, once I actually start, it turns into a physical feeling of losing control where I literally feel like I can't stop myself, even when I'm telling myself to stop.
Can you describe the exact moment when you feel like you lose control during these eating episodes, and is there anything specific that triggers this loss of control?

The loss of control usually starts right after I finish a normal dinner, when I begin picking at leftovers in the kitchen to fill the quiet of the empty house. Once I start, it's like I'm watching myself grab one thing after another, telling myself, "Magin, stop," but I just can't until everything is gone or I'm in pain.
Do you think that if the emotional issues of loneliness and emptiness were effectively addressed, the feeling of losing control during eating episodes would significantly decrease or disappear?

I think addressing the loneliness and emptiness from my divorce and my kid moving out would definitely help, since I've been using food to fill that quiet void. But right now, it's hard to imagine the loss of control completely going away because the urge feels so overpowering once it starts. Still, getting to the root of that quietness feels like it would make a big difference.

Do you believe that the loss of control during eating episodes is more closely tied to the emotional distress of loneliness and emptiness, or has it become a distinct issue that would persist even if the emotional triggers were addressed?

It definitely started as a way to fill the loneliness and quiet of the empty house after my divorce and my youngest child moved out. But once I actually start eating, the loss of control feels like its own powerful force where something just takes over and I can't stop, even when I'm telling myself to. Because of that, I'm not sure if it would just go away if the loneliness did, since the habit feels so incredibly strong on its own now.
Do you experience any other behaviors or habits in your daily life where you feel a similar loss of control, or is this feeling of losing control unique to these episodes of eating?

I haven't really thought about it, and I'm not sure if I feel that way in other parts of my life. But I do know that this feeling of losing control is incredibly strong and noticeable when it comes to my eating in the evenings.

Have you experienced a significant decrease in interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, outside of your hobbies like gardening and fishing, since the onset of your eating issues and divorce?

No, I haven't really lost interest in those activities. I've just been turning down invites to watch the game or grab dinner with my buddies because I'm embarrassed about my eating habits and feel too sluggish the next day. It's more about hiding my situation from them than not wanting to go.
Do you feel sad or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, aside from the feelings of guilt and shame after eating?
No, I don't really feel sad or depressed most of the day. Those feelings are mostly tied to the evenings when the house gets quiet, and especially right after I finish eating and feel that shame.
Can you tell me if there are any days when you don't experience these episodes of uncontrollable eating, and if so, what is different about those days compared to the ones when the episodes occur?

To be honest, there really aren't any days where I don't experience this. Ever since I started my office and mentorship role, these eating spells have been happening pretty much every night, at least several times a week without any real break. Because it happens so consistently, there aren't really any "different" days where I'm free from it.

Do you think your uncontrollable eating episodes would completely stop if you were in a different environment, such as being around others in the evenings, or do you believe the urge to eat would still be present?

I'm not quite sure about that, to be honest, as I haven't really thought about whether the urge would still be there in a different setting. Lately, I've mostly just been avoiding being around other people in the evenings because I'm so embarrassed by my behavior.
Can you clarify if you've experienced a persistent feeling of sadness or depression that lasts throughout the day, not just in the evenings or after eating episodes?

No, I wouldn't say I feel persistently sad or depressed throughout the day. My feelings of shame and regret are really just tied to the evenings and the aftermath of my eating episodes. During the day, when I'm busy with my mentoring work, I actually feel pretty decent.
